qc/runs/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r2/raw-evidence-index.json (input_sha256 matches; recomputed sha256 of results/polish.json and results/golden-1440.png match the index)
evidence: Type fit is correct. Gates: render (1 criterion) and constraints (2 criteria) are all type=binary with aggregation=all_pass (tests/gates/render/judge.toml:16-21, tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:14-33). Functional: all 38 criteria are type=binary under weighted_mean (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:21 and 38 'type = "binary"' lines, no likert); each is a conjunctive pass/fail behaviour with explicit 'Fails if'. Polish: 6 binary criteria (tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:20,29,38,47,56,65), each an observable pass/fail behaviour (keyboard reachability and focus ring, textual feedback, focus return, Undo/Redo disabled state, unsaved marker, 390px usability) with stated fail conditions; this matches the template, whose polish criteria are also binary. None is a craft or degree-of-quality judgement forced into binary. Visual: 3 criteria are type=likert, points=5 (tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:20-21,35-36,50-51) and each has a described anchor on its own line for every level 5,4,3,2,1 (lines 25-29, 40-44, 55-59); they grade degree of craft (editor readability, workspace layout, component finish), not pass/fail behaviour, and are kept apart from each other by explicit scope sentences. Per the skill's known false positive, the workbook internal annotation ('Likert we dont use') is not applied against the shipped likert format. Residual inconsistency (the reason for Note with risk): the frozen template defines a 0-5 scale - every visual criterion has a '0:' anchor (template tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:34) and the prompt has an 'Explicit 0-5 scale' section stating that RewardKit's generic 'integer from 1 to 5' hint is boilerplate and the 0-5 anchors are authoritative (template tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:34-42, 47-48). The task dropped both the 0 anchors and that section, yet tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:5 still says 'assign 0 to every criterion' on gate failure and line 19 says 'the lowest score you can justify'. So the one score the prompt instructs outside 1-5 has no anchor and contradicts the un-overridden 1-5 schema hint. Anchors are also terse at the extremes of cw_visual_component_finish ('5: coherent and polished.', '2: broadly rough.', lines 55, 58), giving the judge little to separate 2 from 3. Not measured: no configured LLM judge run exists (raw-evidence-index.json scope: scripted golden only; 'Visual ratings ... are not measured'), and harbor-rewardkit 0.1.7 source is not available locally, so how a 0 on a points=5 likert is accepted/normalised, and whether an anchor-1 score maps to 0 or 0.2, is unverified. What the task does well: clean separation of behaviour (binary) from craft (likert), anchors on separate lines, and explicit instructions not to score features or palette taste in the visual dimension.
counterexample: Plausible weak app: gates pass but the app's surfaces are unstyled browser defaults; the judge scores each visual criterion 1 ('default browser styling throughout'). If RewardKit normalises score/points, visual = 0.2 rather than the 0 the template's 0 anchor would give, i.e. 0.04 reward mass for absent craft. Conversely, on an in-dimension gate failure the judge is told to output 0 while the schema hint says 1-5; it may emit 1 or RewardKit may reject 0. Both outcomes are unmeasured, impact is small because the render gate already zeroes non-loading apps.
suggested_fix: Either restore the template's convention (add a '0:' anchor to each of the three visual criteria and the 'Explicit 0-5 scale' paragraph in tests/scored/visual/prompt.md), or keep 1-5 and change prompt.md:5 to 'assign the lowest anchor (1)'; optionally add one concrete observable to the 5 and 2 anchors of cw_visual_component_finish. Confirm the 0/1 normalisation in one configured judge run.
